page_title: Dimble: hide and tidy menu bar icons on macOS 27

sources.entry: Dimble - Menu bar manager built for macOS 27's rebuilt menu bar. Hides the icons you don't need until you do. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/fif7y/dimble) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: Dimble
summary.one_liner: Dimble is a free, open source, native macOS app that hides menu bar icons and brings them back on a hover, click, or keyboard shortcut.
use_cases: Declutter a crowded Mac menu bar
Hide rarely used menu bar icons until needed
Find and open a hidden menu bar icon by name
Give an app its own menu bar launcher icon
Access overflow icons macOS had no room for
summary.what_it_does: Dimble sorts menu bar icons into Visible, Hidden and Always Hidden sections, which you arrange by dragging in an editor or by holding Command and dragging in the bar. Hidden icons slide back out when you hover over the bar or click the chevron. Hidden icons can also be shown as tiles in a panel under the bar, where a click opens the real icon's menu. A keyboard shortcut (Option-Command-K) lets you type a few letters to find and open any icon. It can also give any chosen app its own menu bar icon, and offers reveal animations (Instant, Smooth, Fade).
notable: Hidden icons shown as tiles in a panel under the menu bar
No account, analytics or server; only checks for its own updates
Option-Command-K to search and open any icon by name
caveats: Screen Recording permission is optional and only used for reveal animations
